categories.main_business_segments: Samsung SDI operates primarily in two business segments: Energy Solutions and Electronic Materials. The Energy Solutions segment produces and sells lithium-ion secondary batteries including medium, large, and small batteries used in electric vehicles, energy storage systems (ESS), smartphones, wearable IT devices, and power tools. The Electronic Materials segment manufactures and sells semiconductor and display materials such as semiconductor materials, LCD materials, OLED film materials, and polarizing films.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced lithium-ion battery technologies focusing on high capacity, high output, and safety for automotive and energy storage applications. It employs complex manufacturing processes integrating materials, design, and assembly technologies. In electronic materials, Samsung SDI develops coating and film technologies for semiconductors and displays, including high-performance adhesives and quantum dot inks. The company also invests in next-generation battery technologies such as all-solid-state batteries and advanced electrode materials through in-house R&D and collaborations with global research institutes.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include major automotive manufacturers like BMW, Volkswagen, Stellantis, and Hyundai, as well as Samsung Electronics and Samsung Display in the IT sector. The primary markets served are electric vehicles, energy storage systems, smartphones, IT devices, and industrial power tools. The company also supplies semiconductor and display material manufacturers globally. The automotive battery market is driven by regulatory policies on emissions and electric vehicle adoption, while the electronic materials segment serves the semiconductor and display industries.
categories.geographic_coverage: Samsung SDI operates globally with subsidiaries and production facilities in South Korea, the United States, Hungary, Malaysia, China, Vietnam, Germany, and Austria. Its headquarters is located in Yongin, South Korea. The company has manufacturing plants in domestic locations such as Ulsan, Cheonan, Cheongju, and Gumi, and overseas facilities in key markets including North America, Europe, and Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Samsung SDI operates primarily in the midstream segment of the supply chain as a manufacturer and supplier of lithium-ion batteries and electronic materials. It sources raw materials such as cathode active materials and coatings, manufactures battery cells and modules, and supplies these to downstream customers including automotive OEMs and electronics manufacturers. The company also engages in joint ventures for material production, indicating involvement in upstream supply chain activities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in high-capacity, high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles and ESS, rapid charging technologies for IT batteries, and next-generation all-solid-state batteries. It focuses on enhancing battery safety, lifespan, and performance through advanced materials and electrode design. In electronic materials, Samsung SDI emphasizes rapid response to customer needs, development of differentiated semiconductor and display materials, and strategic collaborations to maintain technological leadership. The company also invests in sustainability initiatives such as closed-loop recycling and carbon footprint reduction.
categories.revenue_model: Samsung SDI generates revenue primarily through the sale of lithium-ion battery products and electronic materials. Sales are made directly to major customers and through limited distribution channels. Revenue streams include product sales of battery cells, modules, and electronic materials for automotive, industrial, and consumer electronics applications. The company also earns income from joint ventures and equity-method investments.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Samsung SDI is positioned as a leading global player in the lithium-ion battery industry, competing with companies such as LG Energy Solution, CATL, Panasonic, and SK Innovation. In electronic materials, it competes with specialized suppliers in semiconductor and display materials. The company maintains a competitive edge through technological innovation, strategic partnerships with major automotive and electronics companies, and a diversified global manufacturing footprint.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Samsung SDI achieved record sales of approximately 22.7 trillion KRW, representing a 12.8% increase from the previous year, with an operating profit of about 1.63 trillion KRW, a 9.7% decrease year-over-year. The Energy Solutions segment accounted for nearly 90% of sales, showing significant growth, while the Electronic Materials segment experienced a decline. The company’s total assets reached over 34 trillion KRW, with a stable capital structure reflected by a 58.5% equity ratio and a 71.0% debt ratio. Samsung SDI continues to invest heavily in capacity expansion and R&D to sustain growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Samsung SDI emphasizes high safety, high energy density, and high output in its lithium-ion batteries, catering to stringent automotive and energy storage requirements. Its competitive differentiation lies in advanced battery technologies, strong customer relationships with leading global automakers and electronics firms, and a comprehensive product portfolio spanning small to large batteries. In electronic materials, the company leverages close technical collaboration with customers and continuous innovation to deliver differentiated semiconductor and display materials. Sustainability initiatives and closed-loop recycling further enhance its value proposition.
